why: If you unlock the first k reels, you must pay all k first-viewings, and every remaining m - k viewing should be a rewatch of the cheapest repeatWatch among those k. So the answer is min over k of prefixSum(initial+repeat) + (m - k) * prefixMin(repeat): a greedy scan, no heap needed despite the week's Heap + Greedy label.
hints: Fix how many reels you unlock. Once that prefix is fixed, which reel should every extra viewing go to?
With prefix k unlocked, all extra viewings go to the cheapest repeat cost in that prefix. Cost(k) = sum of (initial[i] + repeat[i]) for i < k, plus (m - k) * min repeat in the prefix.
Scan k = 1..min(n, m), maintaining the running sum and running minimum, and take the best Cost(k). O(n) time, O(1) space; use big integers since m and costs reach 1e9.
pitfalls: You can unlock at most m reels (each unlock is itself a viewing), so k <= min(n, m).
Totals reach about 1e18, so in typed languages use 64-bit integers.
Unlocking more reels is not always better: a later cheap repeat may be too expensive to reach.
